claim.summary: Over a field k, let X_t be a finitely generated FI-set of variables (every variable in the image of X_s for s<=r) and Gamma_t polynomial systems on X_t such that every injection carries the axioms of degree <=D of Gamma_t into the degree-D closure of Gamma_t'. Then the induced substitutions carry closures into closures; the windows Q_t = V_K/(C_D cap V_K) form an FI-module generated in degree <=rK; for fixed polynomials F on a fixed index set with deg w + K <= D the common kernels form a sub-FI-module under injections fixing it; by Church-Ellenberg-Farb-Nagpal (arXiv 1210.1854, its Noetherian property and polynomial-dimension theorems) both dimensions are eventually polynomial over any field. The product and functional pigeonhole systems at fixed holes are such families in the pigeons; holes are functorial contravariantly by setting new variables to 0. For the product pigeonhole systems with K<D<=n the windows have the basis of distinct-hole monomials, dim Q_m = sum_{s<=min(K,n)} binom(n,s) m^s for every m, and along the diagonal m=t+1, n=t the hole-axiom windows form an FI-module agreeing with Q for t>=D, of dimension sum_{s<=K} binom(t,s)(t+1)^s there.

claim.summary: Over any field (multilinear ring, or Boolean axioms among G), let G and P be finite sets of polynomials, H the degree-D PC closure of G, P_D the members of P of degree exactly D, and every member of P of degree >= D. The degree-D closure of G with P equals H + span P_D, with the same members of degree below D as H, if and only if (H + span P_D) cap V_{D-1} lies in H; it suffices that the degree-D parts of P_D are linearly independent modulo the degree-D parts of members of H. For the product pigeonhole system over any field (pigeon axioms prod_j(1-x_ij) of degree n, hole axioms) and D <= n, H is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of the hole-respecting assignments and the closure's members of degree below D are those of H.

claim.summary: Cell splitting: over any field, for any set Q of column-injective assignments of m rows to N holes (e.g. cut by W clauses on arbitrary cell forms) and a column j, with fibers Q^{(empty)} and Q^{(i)} (row i at column j) on the other holes and rho_j = sum_i x_ij, the vanishing tops A(Q) in the weak top algebra T have a filtration by row-sum submodules with factors (1) sum_i x_ij (x) A(Q^{(i)}), (2) rho_j (x) A(Q^{(empty)})/(A(Q^{(empty)}) cap cap_i A(Q^{(i)})), (3) cap over all states of A(Q^{(s)}); hence V(Q) = T/A(Q) is an extension of T'/cap_s A(Q^{(s)}) by (sum_i x_ij V(Q^{(i)}))/(image of factor 2), and the Koszul condition of thm:global-closure-gluing for Q through D follows from it for the row fibers through D-1, Tor_1 of T'/cap_s A(Q^{(s)}) through D, and an (L)-type injectivity for factor 2, over Lambda_{m-1} in characteristic p (the row fibers lie in occupancy class m-1); only the row-fiber condition recurses on sets, and working on the quotient side avoids the socle shift of the ideal-side route. Generalizes lem:hole-splitting (u = m-1, after a change of basis in column j) to cell forms.
